thag3.7:3.1: I read _sikkhetha_ as second person plural optative, and _subhāsitassa_ (etc.) as dative (of purpose), although we would expect the _āya_ form in this sense. The commentary glosses with third singular and accusative (_subhāsitaṁ sikkheyya_). However, this flattens this verse into the same third person voice as the previous two. Its distinctive diction, together with the fact that it exists as a separate verse at [sn2.1:2.1]() (where, further, it appears to be a quotation), suggest its separate origin and purpose.
